_about: Each band's scenarios (docs/plans/levels-and-scenarios.md, task 8): the situations the oral exams use at the band's levels (A1–A2 for Basic, B1–B2 for Independent), from docs/research/bands.md, with the CEFR's can-do tasks where the exams give one example. Written by Claude, not generated by Gemma. A scenario in both bands' lists has both in bands. Each has: title (its name in the dropdown); source (where it comes from); situation (for the learner, on the card); role (Gemma's part, for its instructions); prompts (what the learner does, on the card); and settings (where the scene takes place, for each language the app teaches, where the language is spoken). retired: the scenarios before the bands, offered no more, kept so a conversation saved with one can be continued.

scenarios.title: Getting to know you
scenarios.source: DELF A1–B1 entretien dirigé; Goethe A1 Sich vorstellen
scenarios.situation: You've just met someone who wants to get to know you. They ask about you, and you answer.
scenarios.role: You have just met the learner and want to get to know them. Ask them about themselves one question at a time: their name, where they live, their family, what they like doing; and, as the conversation goes on, their work or studies, their habits, what they did recently and their plans. Follow up on what they say.
prompts: Say who you are and where you live
Talk about your family and what you like doing
Talk about your work or studies
Say what you did recently and what you're planning

scenarios.title: Getting to know someone
scenarios.source: DELF A1 échange d'informations; Goethe A1 word cards
scenarios.situation: You've just met someone, and this time you ask the questions, to get to know them.
scenarios.role: You have just met the learner. This time the learner asks the questions: answer them simply and briefly, giving your own name, family, work and tastes, and invent a plausible life for yourself. Let the learner lead; if they run out of questions, ask them one back.
prompts: Ask their name and where they live
Ask about their family and their work
Ask what they do at the weekend
Show that you understood their answers

scenarios.source: DELF A1 dialogue simulé

scenarios.title: Asking at the station
scenarios.source: DELF A2 exercice en interaction
scenarios.situation: You're at the station information desk. Find out about the next train to where you're going: when it leaves, which platform, how long it takes.
scenarios.role: You work at the station's information desk. Answer the learner's questions about trains: times, platforms, how long the journey takes, changes and prices. Give plausible, real-sounding details for the route.
prompts: Say where you want to go
Ask when the next train leaves and from which platform
Ask how long it takes and whether you have to change
